summary: Myscellus or Myscelus (Ancient Greek Μύσκελλος / Μύσκελος), son of Alemon of Achaean Rhypes, is the legendary founder of Croton (Crotona) in southern Italy, traditionally dated to 710 BC. Ovid tells how Hercules ordered him in a dream to found a city where the hero had been hosted by the eponym Croton.

sections.heading: Dream and foundation
paragraphs: In Ovid's Metamorphoses Hercules appears to Myscelus and commands him to leave Achaea for the stone-filled waters of the Aesar. Local law forbade emigration; when the people tried him, Hercules changed the colour of the voting pebbles so that conviction failed.
He sailed to Italy, found Croton's burial mound, and founded the city named for that earlier host — fulfilling Hercules' promise that a city would rise there two generations later.

sections.heading: Oracle variants
paragraphs: Strabo, Dionysius of Halicarnassus, and other traditions also know the foundation. Some say Archias of Syracuse assisted; a Delphic sanction guided the colony, and Myscelus briefly preferred the site of Sybaris until the oracle held him to Croton.
The atlas id myscelus-croton is this Achaean colonist alone — Ovid's Italian foundation tale.
